source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: What did the lecture recommend for writing a skill that needs real code behind it, such as the video-frame-extraction script in the lecture-notes skill?

options.text: Write it in plain chat, since a chat session writes code as well as any other tool
options.feedback: Chat is fine for a skill that is only instructions, but a skill that has to run and test Python needs a tool built for that, and chat is not one.

options.text: Ask a chat session for the code, then paste the files into the skill folder yourself
options.feedback: You can certainly get code out of chat, but nothing there runs or tests it, so you find out whether it works only when it fails inside the skill. That missing test loop is the whole reason a coding-capable agent was recommended.

options.text: Write it with a coding-capable agent such as Claude Code or Codex, which can test it
options.feedback: Those tools are built to write software and then actually run it, which is what a skill leaning on Python -- here, pulling frames out of a video -- needs behind it.

options.text: Write it by hand in a text editor, since an agent cannot be trusted with its own code
options.feedback: Hand-writing is always possible, but it was not the recommendation, and it gives up exactly the write-then-test loop that makes a coding-capable agent worth using.
